item.title: Re: LLUN Man Seeking Greenlight
item.content:encoded:
(This started as a reply above, but jumping down to a new chain so it's not so horizontally compressed.)

I suppose something I could do is to eliminate all narrative/reasoning portions from this concept and only put down what he is and what he is capable of doing.

That would be the opposite of progress here.

There isn't really a section in the template for SCP Abilities.

Correct. There is a reason for this. SCPs are not merely strange things with lists of abilities, they are stories.

+ my suggestion for where to go from here
- Chisel until the parts that don't look like a statue are gone.

First things first, pitfall wise, you're 100% looking at walking a tightrope over Edgelord Canyon here. This guy could easily tip over into the abyss of edgy 90's comic book characters that have names spelled with statistically disproportionate quantities of "x"s and "y"s… but if you can make this guy a rounded, grounded character it could actually work.

I can see a glimmer of raw diamond here, but the gem metaphor applies heavily: the jeweler's task is all about precisely cutting away the extraneous material to leave only the most interesting parts.
Reading through what you've said so far, I spot the makings of a viable elevator pitch that makes my ears perk up-

  • "He doesn't see someone's destiny. He sees their "supposed" destiny, or what it is that they were meant to do in life, the thing that they are driven towards or driven to do."
  • "wears an assortment of anomalous artifacts that are melded with his body."
  • Jack is a part of Twist's mind
  • the general idea of him pursuing a greater, possibly even benevolent, goal in this hunt he's on

The first one is all the anomaly you need to set you up with an interesting character: A guy with a simple but potent ability chasing pieces of a domino chain that could lead to a cataclysmic end scenario that isn't necessarily going to happen.

Not necessarily suggesting any direct/overt connection, but I immediately jump to SCP-4239- (one of the GAW's Misters Against Weed, Mr. Destiny). His anomaly enables people to find their destiny in this exact sense- not a predetermined fate, but rather their driving purpose and their potential for doing the right thing at the right time to set further things in motion. Mostly just pointing it out as an interesting opposite thematically, but there's also big-picture potential for them to at least have intersecting interests at some point.

But back to the current idea: to riff off of what Cybersquid said, the interest here for me lives in that ambiguous intersection and contrast of "Twist is a ruthless murderer chasing shadows that might only exist in his own head" and "Twist is an anti-hero who will stop at nothing to prevent the destruction of the world". He's not an all-knowing unstoppable monster… just a man who sees a little more than others, with an obsession that may or may not be justified, and a few tricks up his sleeve.

Regarding the grab bag of grafted-on anomalies, the bootleg cyborg thing is a vibe I'm personally a fan of in general, but in this case keep it grounded. A laundry list of abilities isn't going to interest the audience, and pulling out a new gadget every two minutes to do exactly whatever he wants is cartoon supervillain territory. Use simple things in a clever way, though and you paint a picture of a resourceful and competent threat building on past successes.

You've got a great way to organically tie this part of his concept back into the rest, making it even more interesting and playing up that "magnificent bastard" aspect at the same time: What if he can see the potential in things, too? You could get a ton of milage out of having most of his collection being the sort of thing you'd see on the Anomalous Items List, combined in clever ways because he can see their potential. This can complicate his moral standing in odd ways, too- say, he knows that item A vastly increases his ability to stop the cataclysm, but item A is a piece of paratech in the head of a particular unimportant CotBG member.

More flashy components could also be used to hint at past exploits, or even as the basis for tales in themselves. One suggestion I'd throw out is that SCP-748-5 instances (I won't spoil the non-essential details) have integrated phasing tech- the catch being that their tech self-destructs on termination so the unit would have to be alive functional during the transplant process, and that it's probably not going to be the most stable item in his kit even if both he and the device survive the process.

Lastly, while the "tightrope over Edgelord Canyon" warning remains the big flashing red danger sign here, I'd strongly recommend embracing the edginess a little bit if you go the tale series route- like there's some great potential for zombie-stomping action-horror here if you can keep it on the rails in the process.

item.title: Boulevard of Broken Dreams
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Emotional

Page Layout: The "standard" SCP article format, with a description and then test logs hidden in a collapsible. The test logs will be formatted:

 Subject: Items: [Location]:Item ... Afterwards:

Elevator Pitch: A road on which objects relating to your past dreams, goals, and desires appear (out of reach). As you walk along it, past burdens are "freed" from you.

Central Narrative: Disconnected stories of the people that walk on the road, told by the objects that they encounter. For instance:

  • An burnt out ethics committee member who wanted to "bring justice" when he was younger (a discolored robe, a trap with a hole in it, a corroded pen,…, a colorless foundation site), after stepping off of the road he resigns from the foundation.
  • A terrorist who was a revolutionary. (A torn police cap, burnt money, a rusted guillotine,…, his own corpse), who puts up less resistance after.
  • A doctor who wanted to save lives. (A firefighter coat, a broken down gravestone,…, a hospital in the distance). Returned to foundation work with increased score on the Foundation Personnel Wellness Exam.
  • …
+ show block
– hide block

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This SCP aims to tell the story of people's lives through the test logs, which are just lists of items, without the "human" in them. There are no notes on theorized meanings, and the reader is free to draw their own conclusion from the objects and their location on the road.

Additional Notes: I don't quite know how "strong(?)" to make the effect of giving up your past dreams yet. I also don't know if I want to go for the more metaphorical meaning with the items (a clipped bird symbolizing lack of freedom, etc.) or with objects that they used to try to achieve their dreams (the gavel of a judge, etc.).


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts. ~Zyn

I don't really understand why this anomaly would ever be relinquished for the purposes identified in the logs. It seems like the scip would make for a uniquely terrible password due to its anomalous properties, and none of the other proposed uses make sense to me either. (That may be my fault as a reader.)

It was an enjoyable and entertaining read, and your inventiveness is admirable, but I feel obligated to novote the SCP, just because all the relinquishing seems like the opposite of containment. I personally think that experiments should only be conducted (a) when there's some concern about containment procedures potentially being insufficient, or (b) when a specific and explicitly identifiable beneficial result is predicted as the likely outcome (let me tell you about how I'm maybe the only reader who doesn't like the SCP-914 logs…).

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Writers
item.content:encoded:
Hello there, Stonewood. Welcome to the SCP Wiki!

Glad to see after some time of being interested in the topic, you've found yourself interested in writing an SCP of your own. Seeing that you're very interested in writing, I highly suggest that you check out our IRC Chatrooms where you can talk to other members of the community regarding things that interest you. Anyway, here are some resources to help you out around the site:

◎ Open Resources ◎
◉ Close Resources ◉

If you're going to try your hand at writing, try out our sandbox. You can make yourself a page here to store your drafts.

Sandbox

For hashing out concepts, try out the Ideas and Brainstorming forum. You can run your ideas by the community if you need help refining your concept.

If you have a draft ready, make a thread in the Drafts and Critiques forum. Remember to check the stickied posts in the relevant thread for guidelines on how best to use each forum. You can also try the IRC chat for real-time feedback.

From site usage to writing tips, the Guide Hub contains a wealth of resources geared towards helping members produce successful articles.

The more time you take to familiarize yourself with the SCP style, the drafting process, and the community, the greater your chances are for success!

As far as reading is concerned, you might want to check out our Top Rated New Pages, which will display the most popular, recent articles. It's helpful to keep up with what's being received well by the community.

With that said, I hope you enjoy your time here.

item.content:encoded:
The following entries were pruned from this page:

+ show block
- hide block

Event Description: Five sperm whales blew up in size, broke through the surface of the water, until they exploded in large amounts of confetti
Date of Occurrence: 12/12/2012
Location: ██████, Canada
Follow-up Actions Taken: Bodies examined and incinerated. Seeing as the event was near a foundation site, there was no need for amnestics.

The entry is a retread of a previous entry about a volcano, which executed the idea in a more interesting way.

Event Description: At approximately 19:00 hours, foundation geological audio sensors within Veryovkina Cave, Georgia known officially as the world’s deepest cave measuring at roughly 2,212 meters deep began to pick up faint audio around 2,150 meters. Audio recordings after analysis by foundation researchers indicated that several male and female voices were the sources of the previously unknown audio, the voices are thought to be singing 4th Century AD Georgian folk music previously unknown to any modern records. Singing abruptly stopped around 33 minutes later and no known occurrences have happened since.
Date of Occurrence: 8/██/201█
Location: Veryovkina Cave, Abkhazia, Georgia
Follow-up Actions taken: Limited use of Amnestics due to the depth of said site and the fact that all ongoing expeditions below 1,500 feet had been suspended because of high amounts of rainfall in the area. Audio was immediately received by foundation researchers after normal audio was disrupted and two agents have been posted until 202█ to monitor the area for any further activity.

Entry is long-winded and possesses several SPaG errors.

Event Description: A Caucasian male wearing a business suit, and carrying a brief case was seen manifesting randomly throughout the city of ██████, however no persons has shown any recollection of the event. The following day, in the city of ████████, the same event occurred, and again in ████.
Date of Occurrence: ██-██-████
Location: ██████, ████████, and ████
Follow-up Actions Taken: The Foundation confiscated all footage displaying the event occurring, and Class B Amnestics were given to witnesses.

This concept isn't very interesting and isn't very anomalous to begin with.

Event Description: A pickpocket, on the run from local police, ran into an alley and hid underneath a cardboard box. Upon entering the alley and encountering the box, the pursuers appeared to lose interest and continued their search, despite the obviousness of the pickpocket's chosen cover (no other objects of sufficient size to hide an adult were present).
Date of Occurrence: 14/12/2020
Location: San Diego, California, United States
Follow-up Actions Taken: Camera footage showing the event was confiscated under a cover story of the cameras needing maintenance. Police involved in the event were interviewed. None of them seemed to find the event unusual in any way, even when shown video of the pickpocket hiding under the box. Following interviews, those involved were amnesticized. The pickpocket has not yet been located but has classified as a Person of Interest.

Reference to external media and the event itself is barely anomalous.


Forum category: Per Page Discussions / Per page discussions
Forum thread: Log of Extranormal Events

I feel like this SCP succeeded at establishing the tone 5104 attempted. (Note: I'm currently reading batches of SCPs in numerical order. I know 5104 and 5106 are not related.) The Foundation agents here are a bit fumbling, but their behavior is roughly within the bounds of plausibility; they underestimated their opponent, didn't take its cleverness seriously, and let their guard down.

This has some plausibility issues too (how did 5106 figure out how to deploy a sophisticated weapon designed specifically for human use that it had only discovered moments earlier, with no opportunity for practice or experimentation?), but all the same, I'm a bit sad to see 5104 has about three times as many upvotes.

item.title: Joke SCP idea
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: Joke SCP

Page Layout (Optional): A description and various logs of reactions to this SCP's effect

Elevator Pitch: A USB that gets put in successfully the first time you try it. That's it.

Central Narrative: Description along with logs of various reactions to the SCP's effects, including orgasms, screaming in joy, and exclamations such as "MY LIFE IS COMPLETE!" or "ALL THAT MANKIND HAS DONE HAS LEAD TO THIS!"

Hook/Attention-Grabber: People always joke about putting a USB stick the right way in never happening. So I thought "Hey, why don't we put on the ol' Foundation spin on it?"

Additional Notes: It is very likely that this has been done before. Please tell me if it has, and if it has, give me a link because I would very much like to read it if it has been done before.

item.title: [Seeking Greenlights] The last desire.
item.content:encoded:
I hope to convince the authorities of my concept for an SCP I designed. Happy reading/ Christmas/ New Year!!

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout (Optional): The standard Layout for SCPs with two Addendums (an Incident-Report and an psychological report)

Elevator Pitch: The SCP is a immortal person that turns to the SCP Foundation for help. It wants to end its live but cant figure out how.

Central Narrative: Killing this SCP is in the Foundations deepest interest too, because it knows way to much about them (Names/ Protocols/ Top-Secret Data/ …) and threatens to use the knowledge against the Foundation if it wont cooperate. The included documents visualise the struggles and the panic raised by the sudden appearance of this new, serious security thread.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: One of the first details the reader will notice is how little the Foundation knows about the SCP. There will be phrases like: "The subject may be experienced in falsification of psychological tests" or "Instead of us finding it, it found the SCP Foundation". All in all it is a story about the SCP Foundation trying to contain a thread without being able to apply any pressure. The SCP always is one step ahead and doesn't give away this advantage.

Additional Notes: I already have made a final version in the Sandbox, if needed.

item.title: Crime Scene Investigation Procedure
item.content:encoded:
Hey howdy hey, so I'm writing a tale at the moment that predominantly revolves around a crime scene. Thing is, I don't actually know very much about how actual crime scene procedures work, as the most popular point of reference tends to be dramatized TV shows.

I realise that in order to keep stuff interesting I'll need to strike a decent balance between real-world procedure and something a little more fictitious, but I'm not entirely sure where to look for real-world references. I've done some research, but I end up with a mixed bag of results that refer to how various countries handle it.

I'm looking for details of crime scene procedure as it would be in the real world particularly for the US - what kinda staff will be present, who's allowed where, how much can be done on-site that would contribute to the investigation, etc.
The crime takes place indoors (an apartment), and involves a dead body, if those details matter at all.

Articles for reference would be good, and if there's any online short story type deals that exist out there (I've had no luck finding any that aren't books) that would be fantastic.

item.title: Scp of Future Past, and Everything Else...
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:
Scp XXXX is a Reality Bender
Scp XXXX had been discovered in a cave near Quebec, Canada
Scp XXXX is spanned through time and space.

Central Narrative:
Scp XXXX was discovered by an Amateur Cave Explorer in 1973, in a cave near Quebec, Canada. The Amateur Cave Explorer was taken into Foundation custody and amnestisized, alongside all other civilians involved, after reporting to a local hospital, stating he heard a voice in his head talk about freeing himself from the wizards bonds. The Foundation learns Scp XXXX voice spreads into Humans Consciousness when any contact is made beit physical or verbal. The cave of origin is blocked and all Personnel that had been infected had been anesthetized. Scp XXXX is reclassified from euclid to safe. 14 years later, Dr. Mason Cooper reports hearing voices inside his head, though he had only been working for the Foundation for 11 years.

+ show block
– hide block

Staff had concluded that Personnel already infected by Scp XXXX previously had seemed to get reinfected. Though some personnel had either left the Foundation and been Anesthetized or were somewhere else in the world. Scp XXXX is reclassified as keter as it now spreads into the entire world. As more and more instances of Scp XXXX begin to be heard in peoples head the more mist and fog begins to surround Scp XXXX’s point of origin. Until at a Estimated 1 000 000 cases where the fog slowly turned into a human like form and moved into Montreal, Canada. The Foundation theorizes that Scp XXXX was sent across space and time by the Wizards in 1200, so any Instance of Scp XXXX would imbalance its containment as it would be more in one time then the others, meaning it would start to remeterialize. The Foundation enlists Mobile Task Force Simga 32 ( Tbh I Dont Any Good Mtf Who Travel Through Time ) To travel to Canada and release a amnestic and start a PowerGrid Failure to all of Quebec to stop the spread of Media related to Scp XXXX, Finally Sigma 32 puts down a temporal rift near the anomaly, sending all living creatures in the radius to various points in the future in order to contain it. Scp XXXX is currently pending classification of either safe or neutralized.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The archived containment class would go from euclid to safe to keter to pending, meaning there is lots of story.

Additional Notes: If you could help find a name for the Scp Article and a Mtf that specializes in Time Travel I would be even more grateful, but if you just want to critique I'm still very thankful.

item.title: Re: The Bone Seer
item.content:encoded:
Hey there! Thank you so much for taking the time to go through the concept. I'm glad you like the core. Allow me to address some of the points you made.

+ My feedback
- Collapse

I really like this idea of reading the bones but I am unconvinced about the entire thing centred around a vague K-class event. That's no way to build stakes.

I'm trying to go for the idea that the SCP believes it, with the Foundation very much pointing out their scepticism at the validity of the information. This is not at all what the skip would be centred around. It'd serve to introduce the idea that the use of its abilities has shifted its worldview considerably (I mean, even in real life, we have people believing in various apocalypses), with further interviews reinforcing it. However, if you still think that wouldn't work, I get it. Some ideas from the top of my head could be the SCP worried about something/someone "corrupting the Song of the world" and wanting help from the Foundation, but that might be too vague. My (way back) original idea was the SCP being fascinated by the paranormal and wanting to assist and work in the Foundation, but I feared that would be too X-many - something I was terrified of getting close to.

also not convinced that being sure the world would end would then lead to these results… like maybe the cooperation, but why would it make the SCP apathetic about the individual lives? That's fine if you wanna make them cold towards individual lives, but it doesn't make much sense this would be the reason personally.

I was thinking it would be along the lines of "if everyone is going to be dead soon, no reason to get attached or care", or how in an apocalyptic scenario, which the SCP believes in, you'd not get too close to people as they could die at any moment. Still, it could easily be changed to a personality trait gained from being in contact with so many memories, including those of deaths.

I don't think experiment logs are the way to go here. Instead, you could summarize what research was done with the results and then unpack them in conversations or observation reports from the researchers.

I probably worded that part badly since that's what I was trying to go for. The first set of logs would be with the SCP - Foundation giving it various bones and seeing how much info it can gain from them, experimenting with the species of the bones, how old they are, how mundane they are, as well as how accurately the SCP can glean information by cross-referencing the info. The second set of logs would be D-class being given the "charms" and observing how they handle it - a normal person being exposed to memories of, say, a horse, or a murder victim. Also what psychological traits influence how the "charms" affect people (ie. how does someone with would aphantasia deal with having different memories)

I think some unpacking of the actual anomaly would be more interesting than the focus on some vague end of the world.

Again, I think I just phrased it really badly since the other gentleperson above also got that impression. The K-class is by no means the focus of the skip - it's there to explain why the SCP turned in to the Foundation and what motivates it, but beyond the Foundation expressing strong scepticism towards these claims and introducing the idea of the SCP being affected by its abilities, that's it. The meat of the story would very much be talking to the SCP and seeing how its abilities work on it and others.

Please, let me know if any of these replies convinced you/better explained about some part of the skip, or if you're still not sold about some of them working, so I can start thinking of ways to change and modify the concepts. Again, thank you very much for taking the time!

item.title: Re: (Awaiting greenlights) The elite soldier.
item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit
– hide block

The first suit was tested, the U.S. army closed the deal off after they saw what horrible things the suit can do.

What horrible things? There's kinda an implication that this can do many different things but I don't really have a feel for what.

Only 3 were made two are still lost and the third one a soldier still wears.

What does 'lost' mean here? Like, 'missing'? Or 'destroyed'? If it's the first, why is no-one else looking for it?

This feels…a little unsatisfying to me. On one level, there's some thematic weirdness: there's this like, sense that the SCP is a dude who just, wants to do his best and is a big dang hero that everyone loves, except the US army found it too horrifying to use and so there's this disconnect between the angle of 'the foundation will do anything and resort to any means' which feels kinda horrifying and the angle of this dude just being super nice and cool and chill, which feels kinda heartwarming.

On another level: you don't really do anything interesting with this; there's a long investigation section at the start that feels kinda uninteresting because none of the discoveries are particularly novel (since, the discovery would be after the description here: we already know the foundation found a suit and there's a person in it cos guess what, we already read the description) and then there's a vague thing about him joining an MTF. This isn't a bad thing to happen but it's under-utilised: there's no like, extensive training sequence and determined work by the SCP towards convincing the Foundation he can be helpful and uncertainty of whether he'd achieve that; but there's also no real like…cool things happening as a result of them being in a MTF; there's no 'mission log' or anything and I'm left feeling like this just…doesn't have the narrative meat to it for it to work.

Circling back to the themes: I'm really not a fan of the kinda, glorification of the military throughout this. This is, obviously, a personal thing but it's very possible that I just wouldn't like something this 'boo yah go soldiers' even if you had executed it well.

item.title: Buzzcut
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights:Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Fantasy

Elevator Pitch: It's a barber buzzer. Upon using it on one's head, the individual starts receiving more attention than usual. Overtime, as hair grows, the attention diminishes, unless one cuts again, and instead attention increases. Attention, as well as sex appeal. Continuing the process allows the user to have increasing and overwhelming charisma to the extent that they can influence first people, then towns, then world events.

Central Narrative: The buzzer was found to be in the possession of an artifact dealer, and was purchased by the owner of a 50's themed diner to be placed in a safe with other memorabilia. Upon discovery by the Foundation, the dive owner says the girl he bought it from claims it was used by Elvis to cut his hair. After testing the piece is found to be non anamolous, placed in confinement, however an agent over the testing steals it to resell it, but not before trying it on his own head. He begins to notice his life change.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The fact the the influence builds on itself to make the user more and more powerful, and can be transferred if one single hair is buzzed on another man or woman. The buzzer also increases the physical strength of the individual and performance of physiological functions, to the extent that the user can not only become stronger than possible for a human, but also have a faster metabolism (speed), more god like features, and be a far greater sexy badboy/girl than humanly possible.

Additional Notes: After non-use of about a week, all influence dies out. It isn't saved within the buzzer. This is why, if the Elvis fact is true, Elvis, nor any of the other users' influence, is transferred to new users. Any stretch beyond humanly possible abilities granted by the buzzer is unnoticed by individuals, due to the overwhelming charisma, and is brushed off. There is no proper way to cut your hair with the buzzer, but upon doing so, everyone will love your haircut.

I suppose something I could do is to eliminate all narrative/reasoning portions from this concept and only put down what he is and what he is capable of doing.

+ show block

Ok, so here's the problem I'm having right now with this particular project. I'm trying to stay within the template and within the word count. I'm trying not to reveal too much information because if I do, it might seem like a big mess or too much information for someone to swallow in one sitting. The James Devillian Twist SCP project is a big project. I mean… a very big project. He has a wide array of other anomalous abilities and somewhat complicated motivations. He doesn't see someone's destiny. He sees their "supposed" destiny, or what it is that they were meant to do in life, the thing that they are driven towards or driven to do. He sees this along with a ton of other information about that object, including any weaknesses they hold. Twist is a psychopath who will always know how to put his target down.

I read through 049. One major difference here is that through experimentation and interrogation, Twist's "LLUN" threat is verifiable and the second difference is its not a disease. Twist just thinks that if he introduces a small bit of the LLUN's nature to the world, that it might be able to prepare for the upcoming apocalyptic battle with the LLUN, similar to how a vaccine works in a way.

Should I do away with the template and try my own thing with presenting this concept? Use my own format? There isn't really a section in the template for SCP Abilities.

item.content:encoded:
[+] Open for crit

My concern is that there feels like a big disconnect between 'thing what attacks you if you don't run up the stairs in the dark' and everything about there being some kind of breakthrough that could unlock greater human potential, and between that and the tie in to SCP-5000 and Project PNEUMA. It ends up feeling like this has a lot of interesting little ideas in it but not enough connective tissue to hold it all together or to like, explain the jump from one angle to the next.

I'm also not sure if there's enough narrative meat to like, keep us enticed during this process? Like, even if you do manage to have all the information flow together well, it feels…like this really lacking a big narrative hook to really keep us unboard and prevent this feeling like a big info dump about a weird thing. Part of me wonders whether it might work best as a tale focussed around e.g. a foundation researcher who discovers the start of this and then gradually pieces a lot of disparate information together until they discover the truth of this?

I kinda feel like ending on the mystery of what the Foundation learnt might feel really unsatisfying: it kinda feels like the whole thing is built around this mystery and making the reader think about it, and not having a solid answer here feels…like it might end up feeling kinda analogous to reading every chapter of an Agatha Christie book except the final one where you find out who done it.

SCP-XXXX is a computer program that one day appeared and automatically installed in every computer at site-XX.

This feels…a little unsatisfying to me? Iunno, I like the idea of the program spreading through alternative universes and like, letting you control people in other universes, but it feels…purposeless?

I think at the end of the day, the lack of purpose is my biggest issue with this concept: there's some really cool flavour here and I like the idea of the Foundation eventually figuring out that it's not simulating stuff but it feels…like this is the setting of a story where you haven't managed to tease the core narrative arc out yet?

It feels like this needs…a character to focus on say, or for the plot of this to end up going somewhere more than just, revealing more about what this does. The idea of playing with the conflict between 'using this to figure out how to handle containment breaches better' and 'not using this to prevent it spreading and reduce the risk of a containment breach here' could be fun; or a discussion of the ethics of causing harm in another universe instead could be good; but without something like this where it ends up y'know, escalating and coming to some kinda conclusion, I'm not sure it'd work.

item.title: SCP-XXXX A blessed exchange (Seeking greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Horror/Mystery

Page Layout: Object description and containment are minimal, and main focus will be on testing logs. There will be 10-15 of them, starting with mundane, and increasing in strangeness.

Elevator Pitch: The object swaps two aspects (body parts/memories/reality of their life) of a person with a new one, seemingly from its "collection" of obtained aspects. Since an unknown number of exchanges have occurred, over an unknown time/places, it has an unknowable number of aspects in its collection.

Central Narrative: Minimal. The testing logs will add mystery around the objects age/origins and purpose, suggesting alien/extra-dimensional life. Since the object can alter reality, detailed records and logs need to be kept in order to keep track of reality alterations.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The object removes aspects of a person and gives a brand new one. The removal of aspects could kill or dramatically change a person, even removing people/companies/ideas related to them. The new aspects can be memories, new organs, or reality altering itself as well. The testing logs will start with mundane things, eg gaining memories of another person, growing a new limb etc, and will progress to stranger exchanges where friends/family cease to exist, or they gain non-human knowledge. Adding to the intrigue is that every aspect "given" is assumed to have been taken at some stage, suggesting that the object has altered reality many times in the past in unknown ways.
